source_text: propterea vos novos haereticos dici, quia omne malum quod peccatum definitur, asseritis non in natura, sed in sola voluntate consistere egressum, qui in se summam proelii sitam optat intellegi
pass_a_gloss: Propterea you new heretics dici, because every evil that/which sin is-defined, you-assert not in nature, but in alone by-will to-consist having-come-forth, who in himself the-sum of-the-battle placed wishes to-be-understood.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: One man has come forward who wants people to think that the whole battle depends on him.
We are called new heretics because we maintain that every evil defined as sin consists in the will alone, not in nature.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
